title: Food or computers?

predict.q: The economy is at C (20 computers, 75 food). It moves to D (30 computers). What is the opportunity cost of the extra 10 computers?

options.fb: Food falls from 75 to 50: 25 units of food are given up for the extra 10 computers.
That is the food left at D, not the food given up: 75 − 50 = 25.
That is the food you started with. Opportunity cost is the change.

options.s: Nothing: the economy just makes more
options.fb: At C all resources are already in use. More computers means moving resources away from food.

task: Move the **Computers** slider from 20 to 30 and watch the food bar fall from 75 to 50.

target.do: Move the Computers slider from 20 to 30, then press Check.

takeaway: When all resources are in use, more of one good means less of the other. The opportunity cost is the amount **given up**, not the amount left.
explore: Now try 0 → 10 (10 food given up) and 30 → 40 (50 food): the cost rises.
